scenes.spec: interior at a red light — coffee cup in the holder rippling, wheel trembling faintly
scenes.narration: Red light. Foot on the brake. And the car... shivers. The wheel hums in your hands, the coffee ripples like that scene in Jurassic Park, and the moment you pull away — smooth again, like nothing happened. Idle is the engine's hardest trick: keeping sixty-plus explosions a second perfectly balanced with NO throttle to hide behind. Everything that's slightly wrong shows up here first, at the light, in your coffee cup. Which makes rough idle the great early-warning symptom — annoying long before it's expensive, if you listen while it's cheap.

scenes.spec: channel card — "Why Is My Car Doing That?"
three-way split — "Shake in the car, or in the RPM?" / "Cold only, warm only, always?" / "AC on/off change?"
scenes.narration: **Watch the tach at idle.** If the NEEDLE is steady but the CAR shakes, that's a vibration transmission problem — spoiler, motor mounts — not a combustion problem. If the needle itself wanders, dips, or surges, the engine is genuinely struggling. **Temperature pattern.** Rough ONLY cold then smooths warm; rough ONLY warm; rough always. Cold-rough leans rich-mixture and sticky-valve suspects; always-rough leans vacuum and ignition. **Load test at a standstill:** flip the AC on. AC adds load; a marginal idle gets visibly worse. Headlights, defroster — same trick. Note it; it's free evidence. [TECH CONFIRM — bless AC-flip as a useful at-home data point]

scenes.section: THE MECHANISM — WHY IDLE EXPOSES EVERYTHING
scenes.spec: metronome from ep 10 slowed way down — at idle, each combustion event stands alone; one weak beat rocks the whole engine
scenes.narration: At 700 RPM there's no momentum to blur mistakes. Every cylinder's contribution is felt individually; one weak or missing beat rocks the engine on its mounts — the exact lope you're feeling. And because idle airflow is tiny, even a small unmetered leak is a HUGE percentage error at idle while being a rounding error at speed. That asymmetry is why so many problems idle rough but drive fine.

scenes.spec: intake tract from ep 10 — cracked hose, brittle intake boot, failed intake gasket; hiss visualized; idle air % math overlay
scenes.narration: The signature: **rough idle that smooths out the second you rev.** At 700 RPM, a pencil-size leak might be 10% of total airflow — chaos. At 3,000 RPM it's 1% — invisible. The engine bay is full of aging rubber: vacuum hoses, intake boots, gaskets, brake booster line. Shops find leaks with smoke machines — literally filling the intake with theatrical smoke and watching where it escapes. [TECH CONFIRM — smoke test standard at FHT? Price for the callout table]

scenes.section: CAUSE #2 — IGNITION MISFIRE AT IDLE (plugs, coils — the ep-10 suspects, second shift)
scenes.spec: coil/plug stack — weak spark at low RPM, cylinder-specific lope; misfire counter
scenes.narration: Same ignition suspects as the acceleration episode, different shift: a marginal plug or coil that survives cruise can drop beats at idle where combustion is least forgiving. Tell: rhythmic lope (you can almost count the bad cylinder), often a P030X code, sometimes a flashing light at idle. The coil-swap test from ep 10 applies unchanged. scenes.section: CAUSE #3 — DIRTY THROTTLE BODY AND IDLE CONTROL
scenes.spec: throttle body — carbon ring around the plate; airflow strangled at the tiny idle opening
scenes.narration: At idle the throttle plate is nearly closed; the computer meters air through a sliver of an opening. Years of PCV vapors (hello, ep 8) bake a carbon ring exactly where that sliver lives, strangling and destabilizing idle airflow: surging idle, stalls at stops, rough after battery disconnects. The fix is famously satisfying — a cleaning — with one modern caution: electronic throttle bodies want a **relearn procedure** after, or the idle gets worse before it gets better. [TECH CONFIRM — DIY-safe with cautions, or shop job on drive-by-wire cars? Your relearn horror stories welcome]

scenes.spec: NEW insert — engine on its mounts; one collapsed hydraulic mount; vibration path into the frame at idle-in-Drive
scenes.narration: The impostor from the symptom section: tach steady, combustion fine, car still shakes — worst at idle IN GEAR, foot on brake, often smoothing in Park or Neutral. That's a collapsed **motor mount** — the rubber-and-fluid cushions that carry the engine. Free driveway test: idle in Drive, brake held vs Neutral — big difference points at mounts. [TECH CONFIRM — bless the in-gear-vs-neutral test; typical mount job cost range]

scenes.section: CAUSE #5 — FUEL TRIM DRIFT: INJECTORS, SENSORS, AND THE CHECK-ENGINE BREADCRUMBS
scenes.spec: fuel trim graph drifting positive; O2 sensor lazy; one injector dribbling
scenes.narration: The subtle tier: aging **O2 sensors** report lazily, a tired **injector** dribbles instead of misting, the computer chases its own tail, and idle quality erodes gradually — usually with fuel-trim or lean codes as breadcrumbs. This tier is scan-tool territory; the takeaway for viewers is just that gradual-and-getting-worse with brea dcrumb codes is a real, findable pattern, not "cars just do that." [TECH CONFIRM — comfortable keeping this tier brief like this?]

scenes.section: THE REPAIR — WHAT THE MONEY LOOKS LIKE
scenes.spec: decision ladder — steady-tach? mounts. wanders? scan → smoke test → cheap items → sensors
scenes.narration: The fork saves the money: **steady tach + shaking car → mounts** — skip the engine diagnosis entirely. **Wandering tach → scan, smoke test, ignition basics, throttle cleaning** — in that order, cheapest evidence first. Most rough idles die on the first two rungs. scenes.spec: three-tier verdict card — "Annoyance tier" / "Book it" / "Same rules as ep 10"
scenes.narration: **Annoyance tier:** mild, consistent, no codes, no stalls — a mount story or minor leak. Fix on your schedule; it won't strand you. **Book it:** stalling at stops, surging, any code, or the pattern getting worse month over month. Stalls in traffic are a safety issue dressed as an annoyance. **Same rules as ep 10:** flashing light, raw fuel smell — the misfire urgency tiers apply verbatim. [TECH CONFIRM — bless the tiers]

So: idle is the engine with nowhere to hide. The tach sorts real combustion trouble from mount impostors, the rev test fingers vacuum leaks, the AC-flip adds free evidence, and the smoke machine finds what ears can't. Catch it at the coffee-ripple stage and it's almost always bottom-of-the-ladder money. Next time: your car smells like rotten eggs — and the converter that's telling you something died upstream of it.
